samples.summary: Export exit-code test titled "without writing the file" asserts nothing about file writes
samples.evidence: `it('exits 2 on a 401 without writing the file')` (and the sibling 404 case) only assert `process.exitCode`. Nothing checks that `out.pdf`/`out.md`/`out.pptx` were not created, so the second half of the test's claim is unverified — if the early `return` in the error-body branch of `docs/notes/slides export` were removed, the test would still pass (and would silently write files into the test cwd). Also, `expect(process.exitCode).toBe(1)` for the 404 export cases cannot distinguish the new `exitCodeForStatus(res.status)` from the old hardcoded `1`, nor from an unrelated throw funnelled through `outputError` (which defaults to 1); no stderr body is asserted there, unlike the 401 cases.
searchedFor: grep for writeFileSync / existsSync assertions in that file

samples.summary: docs import's "2xx without an id" change from exit 1 to EXIT_SYSTEM_ERROR has no test (notes and slides do)
samples.evidence: `runDocsImport` now returns `EXIT_SYSTEM_ERROR` when a 2xx create omits `id`, and `exitCodeForStatus(...)` for the `--replace` PUT failure. `packages/cli/test/docs-import.test.ts` contains no `INVALID_RESPONSE` case at all (grep found none) and no `--replace` PUT-failure case; the equivalent changes in `notes/import.ts` and `slides/import.ts` did get tests updated to 2. So the docs variant of this behavior change ships untested.

samples.summary: The security warning printed for --allow-unbound-callback (and the listener's 'Accepting a callback with no login state' notice) is asserted nowhere
samples.evidence: `runLogin` prints 'Warning: --allow-unbound-callback accepts a callback that carries no state...' and `startCallbackServer` prints 'Accepting a callback with no login state (--allow-unbound-callback).'. In `packages/cli/test/login.test.ts` the `runLogin` describe does `vi.spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {})` and never inspects the calls; the `allowUnbound` listener tests assert only the HTTP status and resolved code. Deleting either warning would not fail any test, even though the diff's own rationale is that the downgrade must be announced.

samples.summary: registerLoginCommand's new catch/exit wiring is untested; only the pure classifier is
samples.evidence: The action now wraps `runLogin` and does `const exitCode = classifyLoginFailure(e); if (exitCode === null) throw e; console.error(message); process.exit(exitCode)`. `login.test.ts` tests `classifyLoginFailure` directly and `runLogin` with injected deps, but nothing drives the command action, so the wiring (message printed as prose rather than JSON, unclassified errors rethrown with their stack, exit code actually applied) has no coverage.

samples.summary: The multipart/binary endpoints' fetchOrThrow classification is claimed but only the JSON path is tested
samples.evidence: The comment on `send()` states 'every request the CLI makes, including the multipart file endpoints, is classified the same way'. `packages/cli/test/http-client.test.ts` only exercises `listApiKeys`/`createApiKey`/`revokeApiKey` (JSON), including the one 'classifies an unreachable server as a system error' case. No test drives `uploadFileDocument`/`downloadFileDocument` against a rejecting transport, so the binary half of that claim is unverified.

samples.summary: Guard: no test for an unknown non-empty Sec-Fetch-Site value, nor for the warn log
samples.evidence: `assertCliStartNotCrossSite` refuses any value not in `ALLOWED_FETCH_SITES`, i.e. also a typo/unknown token such as 'same-sight' or a future value, and it logs via `this.logger.warn`. The spec covers only 'cross-site' (plain and duplicated), the three allowed values, absent and empty. Nothing pins the unknown-value branch or the log line, so narrowing/widening the allow-list to a pure `=== 'cross-site'` check would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: isOpaqueRedirect's `res.type === 'opaqueredirect'` branch is not exercised; only the status-0 path is
samples.evidence: The only test for the opaque-redirect fallback stubs `fetch: async () => Response.error()`, which yields `type: 'error'`, `status: 0` — it hits the `res.status === 0` disjunct. No test produces a response with `type === 'opaqueredirect'`, so removing that check (the spec-mandated shape the comment says it exists for) would not fail anything.

samples.summary: no_proxy bracketed-IPv6 parsing and lower-case-wins env precedence are untested
samples.evidence: `splitHostPort` has a dedicated `^\[(.+)\](?::(\d+))?$` branch and `envValue` documents 'lower case winning'. The `proxyForUrl` tests cover bare hosts, '.suffix', 'host:port', '*', upper-case spelling and all_proxy fallback, but never a `[::1]:8080` no_proxy entry nor both spellings of the same variable set simultaneously, so neither documented behavior is pinned.

samples.summary: files upload / notes+slides import only test the 5xx→2 direction of exitCodeForStatus, not 4xx→1
samples.evidence: `files-upload.test.ts` `makeClient(false)` always answers 500, and the only status assertion is the changed `exitCode).toBe(2)`. Same in `notes-import.test.ts`/`slides-import.test.ts`, whose fixtures hardcode `status: 500`. A regression that mapped every failure to 2 (e.g. `return EXIT_SYSTEM_ERROR` instead of `exitCodeForStatus(...)`) would pass all of them; only `docs-import.test.ts` added a 400→1 counter-case.

samples.summary: classifiedFontFetch's URL/Request input normalisation is untested
samples.evidence: `classifiedFontFetch` branches on `typeof input === 'string'`, `input instanceof URL`, else `input.url`. The two new docs-export tests inject `fontFetch` and only ever see the string form used by `PdfFonts`, so the URL and Request branches (which decide what appears in the redacted error message) are never exercised.
